facts.text: Manistee Lake sits on an isthmus between Manistee Lake and Lake Michigan, with the Manistee River bisecting the city as it flows west to the latter.
The name 'Manistee' derives from an Ojibwe word meaning 'river with islands at its mouth'.
During the lumber boom of the 1880s, Manistee hosted its own railroad, the Manistee and North‑Eastern, and boasted more millionaires per capita than any U.S. city.
The Ramsdell Theatre, opened in 1938 with Art Deco design, became the first home for actors such as James Earl Jones in Manistee.
Manistee County Historical Museum showcases local heritage, including the North Pierhead Light and the history of Rietz Park.
The surrounding Manistee National Forest offers thousands of acres of forest, farms, and orchards, a hallmark of the region's natural beauty.
